commentBody:
RUNS SCARED. 

Yeah...that's not a phrase. 

("Not all debuts are good" - Rex Parker. )

Beautiful grid! So beautiful, in fact, that I didn't notice it's only 22x22. With fewer squares to fill, that's probably why my solve time was lower than average. These constructors, they're so clever!

Love the premise and the 10-4 construction on 10-4 (which I didn't know was 110A) but I finished it waaaay too quickly! It's so disappointing to basically look at a clue and fill in the answer. Now what am I supposed to do with the rest of my evening? ;) But kudos, Kathryn, on pulling off the structure!

Well, my jaw actually dropped when I first saw this grid. It was kind of a combination smile and jawdrop.  This grid is a piece of beauty! 

I mean look at it!  Ever seen anything like it?  No, you haven’t.

And it’s wonderfully quirky.  Even with an extra column and row, it has 12 fewer words than the usual Sunday.  And the one that really gets me is that the usual Sunday has 74 black squares and this one has 132!

Oh, you rebel, Kathryn, breaking conventions left and right, but finding a theme to justify it.  Hah!  Only words of two lengths!  And making those lengths 10-4, to tie them into National Truckers Day, which falls on this Sunday.

So, let’s see.  You’ve got chutzpah, Kathryn, and you’ve got amazing grid-building skill, and this is your NYT debut.  Wow is all I can say, and I can’t imagine what you might follow this up with – but I want to see it!  Thank you!

The very interesting idea of limiting answers to four letters and ten letters does not overcome my distaste for a Sunday themeless with mostly Monday- and Tuesday-level clues.

(A graph theory theme would have been interesting.)

OK so we can make some fun 10-4 combos from the entries:

CREAMPUFFS NAPS: sort of like that tryptophan thing

TOE THE LINE NUNS: very strict

SIDEGLANCE LOVE: meet-cute in the produce aisle 

REDUCED FAT LOOT: the Halloween rice cakes given out by the quirky neighbors

Any more??

An architectural gem; a crucverbial meh. (Very few clue/answers sparkled with creativity.)

Overall, I hate to do it, 7/10. 

tc

I’ve been retired for a while, but back in the day we referred to physicians in a certain field, and the name of the field itself, by either just saying the letters “O-B-G-Y-N”, e.g. “send a referral to OBGYN” or the phrase ”O-B Gyne” (hard G).  I never heard the word “gyno”. The “o” at the end of that word actually makes it sound a little weird. Google tells me it is also an abbreviation for the condition gynecomastia
A joy based on the construction alone. Fun and zippy with a few clever mis directs. What more could you ask for a Sunday?

Wow! A really impressive debut, Kathryn. I get what many have said/will say—Sunday themelesses are not always much fun, and this one from a solving standpoint has an unavoidable drawback—all those four letter entries. There’s only so much you can do to spiffen those up (I just coined that word) and while some had some fresher clues most didn’t. So the result was I didn’t really get to linger on or appreciate all those interesting 10s. That aside, what a wonderful concept (how long did they have to wait for 10/4 to be on a Sunday?) and it had the feeling of a much more experienced constructor, despite the inherent limitations, so I still had a lot of fun and am duly impressed, looking forward to more. This was actually a very funny coincidence, I just learned about this day because I used it in a puzzle I just submitted as part of a clue for OCT! Had to run the alphabet at SUITOATEE, just couldn’t parse it, luckily everything else was right. Anyone else hear Wesley announcing “To the Pain!” from Princess Bride at 68 down? https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=wUJccK4lV74&ra=m I hope this was a REFLECTIVE enough POST—I thought that was the star clue today! Another Crosshare post. This was one of my earliest puzzles and I'm not so thrilled by all the fill, so I apologize for that in advance. I haven't really seen another theme like this, though, although you can essentially solve it themelessly if you wish. https://crosshare.org/crosswords/fxL0RPeIwsBpHofFsdNF/intersections
I had never heard of solar farts before.🤪
Looking forward to next week. Hopefully, the weekend puzzles get good again.
All too often, these very gimmicky puzzles strike me as giving more joy to the creator than the solver.  But not here. At least for me, there joy is for both.  Well done.

"10/4 celebration ... as suggested by this grid"

...the mess I had in the lower right corner because I took "as suggested by this grid" far too literally and was convinced it was CHECKERDAY for quite a long time (the 4x4 squares looked checkerboard-ish to me).

Anyway, the October 4th holiday I celebrate is Cinnamon Bun Day. I invite you to join me.
Why is EVER’S partner ANON?  Thank you.
congratulations and kudos to Kathryn Bale - this is a crossword classic!

I can’t wait for the boo-birds to come out.  Too much of this or too easy or too natticky. When I first opened this puzzle my eyes did a double take. Could this be the prettiest grid in some time?  Just look at the symmetry. Then to find out that this is a debut submission. I AM IN AWE OF YOUR GIFT. I look forward to your next dazzling display. Thanks for sharing it Kathryn, BRAVA!
Kind ofaletdown
I'm a little late to the game tonight, and I'm shocked--shocked!--that no one has posted the day's anthem: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Sd5ZLJWQmss
we all get the things we need from truck drivers and delivery people the whole supply chain made in to a 10-4 puzzle on oct. 4th that's absolutely brilliant.  it's a true classic - copy that?!
Amazing and so much fun :)

Excellent debut puzzle, Kathryn.

I am very impressed, especially given the constraints you put on yourself in creating this.  

Fine work.
Waste of a Subday puzzle. I hope the constructor had a good time making it.

My first thought, when I saw the grid, was "this looks easy...all those short answers".  

My second thought was terror, realizing there were so many 2x2 sections unconnected with most of the rest of the puzzle--a sure fire way to get completely stuck.

So every time I got a section done I breathed a bit easier.  But I was sure one of them was gonna get me good.
in love with this puzzle for so many reasons - it's who we ARE!

ILOVEDTHIS TONS! 

Before all else, I took a moment to admire and be mystified by the grid design.

And then I had a rollin' good time with the solve, very smooth and satisfying. 

Congrats on and thank you for a beautiful debut, Ms. Bale!

One of my two brothers had a knack for saving money and then spending it on hefty acquisitions that he intended to learn to use but never did (a surfboard, a drum kit, a CB radio...)
Well, the CB radio we did use. Once. 
I was fourteen, he was fifteen, and here we were interrupting the truckers' banter, saying hi. They could tell from our voices that we were young, and they were super careful with their language, refraining from jargon and coarseness and going out of their way to be welcoming and nice. 

Here's a shout-out to all truckers on their day. It can't be easy being on the road with so many bad drivers who never learned that you don't cut in front of a truck. My heart goes out to all of you. :-)
Mostly a fun puzzle with nice symmetry.  NE was kind of ridiculous.  Knowing profiteroles are CREAM PUFFS with some really bad crossings.
Mega funk groove vibes for Trucker's Day, here's Eddie Kedricks with "Keep on Truckin'" - https://youtu.be/iiH73t0OmPI?is=Nfu23w1hWCnxVb9I
Having the word MAIL in the same grid (in crossing answers, no less) was a crossword nono, I thought.
This is probably one of the most fun Sundays I've ever solved. The clues were a bit easy for a Sunday, but the gorgeous grid and clever theme certainly made up for it. Bravo!

Fun puzz.

Now when I try to imagine how to approach the feat of all and only 10s and 4s supersymmetrically I get all vertiginous and tingly and woogly on the back of my legs like when I'm standing at the south rim of the Grand Canyon.

Quite impressive! Unusual grid, and a unique constraint that obviously took some time to assemble.

Nice debut, Kathryn, and hope to see more of your work.
Too many religious references for my taste.
Awesome puzzle. I love the boldness of the 10 / 4 grid!
10-4, good buddy! Loved the unique grid and a lot of the 10-letter clueing. Fast one, too. Keep on trucking.

Guess I'm the party pooper this evening. This puzzle did not spark joy for me. I felt like I was trudging through it. I did like thinking about the Morton Salt girl, a link to my younger self, with her brolly and galoshes. And then wondering are there Morton families and Diamond Crystal families just like there are Skippy and Jif peanut butter family. Jim Horne at xwordinfo.com informs me that there are 96 four letter entries in this puzzle. Here's a song with a tear for each one*. https://youtu.be/xS7qvxm3FbM?si=CIAtW6Z5puDHiH23 *32 10 letter entries

Clever concept but a comparatively easy solve for me. Just over twenty minutes, ten minutes under average. I've never seen a puzzle that looked quite like this one, though. My mind loves symmetry so I enjoyed this puzzle quite a bit. Well done.
That was fun! Thank you!
This is a remarkable achievement. To pull off this grid with clean, fun fill is very very impressive. Love it!!

I know for a fact John Stewart does the ny times puzzle does anyone know if he comments?  again Kathryn and Will Shortz and the editorial team this was truly the way puzzling should be - I can't fathom the difficulty day by day figuring out what works but for sure no A.I. generated puzzles other than checking spelling normal stuff. and bring back long phrases we all adore... BRAVO!

Lots of fun, and the construction was such a clever conceit that never felt too forced. 

Though I must say, the overwhelming majority of MICROSCOPEs can not see viruses, which are too small to be seen with optical microscopes and require more exquisite devices like scanning electron microscopes, so that one threw me a bit, though I realize I may have been too clever by half there!
How do you guys make sure that the puzzles weren’t composed by AI?

It was fine. But it made me appreciate the 21-space clues that so often become tricky companions for the whole journey of solving a puzzle.  At turns confounding and beguiling, and satisfying in the end, an a-ha! moment may arrive only after a sufficient period of suffering!

I don't care whether a grid was a feat of construction. I just want to have an enjoyable solve. Personally I found today's puzzle a bit meh. There were some nice spots with fun misdirection ("Nails will do it, but not teeth"), but most of the clueing was boring and direct. Then there was the area with FI__, AN__, AR__, and MORT__SALT crossing - to me it made for a naticky mess I was only able to resolve with lookups.
I'd never heard of "Trucker's Day" before now. But you can also celebrate Buster Keaton's birthday as well.  :)
This puzzle was clever and fun.  I didn't catch on that all the answers were either ten letters or four until I read column.  Wow!
The clue 27A, "It may be teen or false", is inaccurate. A false idol is an idol that is false, but a teen idol is not an idol that is teen. Better "word with false or teen" or something like that.
All 10s and 4s. Can't even imagine trying to build something like that - and that on a Sunday scale. Well done!

OK, someone please educate me. Is this puzzle themeless? The column says "Today's Theme" but I see posts here saying it's themeless. It seems to me the theme is as the title says, 10-4, with entries about Trucker Day, Sputnik, ten minus four and the structure of the grid. Is this incorrect?

Phenomenal grid (and debut?!) from Kathryn B.

10/4 Grant R. stars

Excellent theme, so many layers. The length of the answers. The direct meanings of 10-4. The date references.
Beautiful grid.
10-4 good buddy.  That was fun.
I guess I am in the minority, but I really disliked this puzzle. Fine construction effort, but dull puzzle. I expect more out of my Sundays.

Pretty amazing puzzle design. 67D was one of my first gets, as my grandmother had gotten a Spaniel around this date and named him Sputnik, but “One” threw me for a bit. I know that some may have found this to be less of a challenge, but I found that the beauty of the layout superseded the need to have all of it be challenging. I also found that sometimes getting the 10-letter answers easier than the 4-letter ones, and that they were the answers that put me on the path to nailing a section. I thought it was a lot of fun—nicely done!
You know what else fits at 110A? mybirthDAY. I was tempted to enter that, because it is. So tickled when I opened it up and saw the title. Enjoyed the solve too. Thanks, Kathryn!

"Tentilfour"
Dolly's lesser known sequel, after her having championed improved office conditions including shortened working days

Well, the grid design certainly grabbed my attention. As expected though, the resulting GLUT of four letter words made the solve less interesting for me. That doesn't negate my appreciation for the feat that Kathryn pulled off, though. Very impressive constuction with such tight constraints. I'm looking forward to what she'll do next. Taj Mahal covering one of my favorite TRUCKER songs: https://youtu.be/1WaHXscnbUw?si=QFQsymRjNzkqIaay
Enough with puzzles whose construction is impressive, but the solving experience unenjoyable. And you told us the revealer in the clue! Why?
ARCO? FICO?

Nice to have this puzzle honoring truckers. It isn't an easy time for them, and the work they do deserves recognition. 

And here's yet another tribute via song. Linda Ronstadt's cover of  'Willin'' by Little Feat.

Enjoyed this Clever construction. 96 reasonable 4 letter words was impressive and no Oreo! I had paper plates before pasta salad for summer cook out dish. Favorite clues were for older pipes and microscope.

A very interesting construction, which must have been quite challenging to create. And despite the significant constraints imposed by the design, the fill seemed rather solid, all in all.

Not especially challenging---about thirty minutes for me---but appropriate and enjoyable to solve.

Congrats on the impressive debut!
wordpuzzle             love
Hello, why is TOPS BEST and not BESTS?
Nice rare Sunday gold. The crosses did their jobs, else I would have never guessed ATEN or TRAD or BESS. Cheers!

How long before Beyoncé and Harry Styles qualify as OLDERPIPES?


Completed this puzzle at exactly 3:50 (somewhere) !!
A beautifully impressive debut, in both form and content.  Thank you!
Unsually easy Sunday, at least for me.

“So when ya see that big truck rollin by Wave yer hand or kinda wink yer eye, Cuz that's Bud the Spud from old PEI, with another big load a’ potatoes!“ https://youtu.be/HtySGSuKZe8?si=itkYMdu6CjZUKc-h

I've finished the NW corner.  It required such little brainpower that I could have planned the next lunar mission while doing it.  If I knew how to plan a lunar mission, that is.  Not a scintilla of challenge or even mini challenge.  So I stopped.

I literally laughed out loud when I saw this grid.

My second thought, after only a few clues, that there would be tons of complaints about the ease of many of the answers.

Well below my Sunday average, a bit above my best, but the fun, coupled with the appreciation for the construction, made it worthwhile.

But seriously, all those four letter words and no OREO?

Amazing puzzle. Good long workout for me, and... just got stuck in a couple of places and couldn't quite work it all out. No big deal - that's just me. And my puzzle find today. A Thursday from November 17, 2016 by Timothy Polin and Joe Krozel. Hard to describe this one, but... some of the answers: PYRAMIDSCHEME TOMBRAIDER PHAROAHANT CAGEDUP TUT And then... One answer was embedded in a pyramid of black squares with no crossing answers. And that answer was: MUMMY Here's that link: https://www.xwordinfo.com/Crossword?date=11/17/2016&h=4d ...

Calling all constructors:  For September 25, a Dolly Parton tribute puzzle.

(With apologies in advance to @Andrzej for the weird American date format.)
43-Down was an evil, evil clue. Reflective Post.  Thought for sure this was "POST MORTEM". Took me forever to finally get it.

Ah yes, another one of those puzzles that seems more fun for the constructor than the solver.  A themeless Sunday in disguise.  I admit, when I first beheld the grid, I was stunned by how much time and effort undoubtedly went into its construction.  But TBH I do Sundays for the wordplay and themes, not to marvel at how pretty the grid looks empty.

A salute to Kathryn on constructing a fantastic grid!  Took me quite a while, but it was both entertaining and challenging.  Early on I had FORMULAONE instead of SPRINTCARS, which led to several other erroneous entries.  Had to abandon the temptation to concentrate on the shorter entries, which were tougher than normal in many cases.  Very unique puzzle.
Now, I can't wait for the puzzle for Sunday April 20 (2031).

This one was fun. Called on my memories of watching BJ and The Bear when I was young. Who knew that would come in handy almost 50 years later!?! My daughter and I managed to finish this one relatively quickly (~90 mins, which is quick for us on a Sunday), so completing it filled me with some pride…well…almost! We cracked all but two clues: the FICO and ARCO intersection. We’re Canadian, and FICO does not operate up here so that entity was totally unknown to me. We could have overcome that barrier had we been familiar with the arcane Italian commands given to players of the violin or other orchestral stringed instruments. But, alas, such is the nature of these NYT crosswords! Looking forward to the next one.

Have you heard of the Iron Goat?

It goes where the Iron Horse can’t. 

Happy Trucker Day to all the Iron Goats out there!!

If you're looking for another puzzle with a fun grid design, you might want to try Liz Gorski's October 18, 2009 puzzle. 
She mentioned it as one of her favorite constructions in a Q&A over at the New Yorker this week.

WARNING: It's somewhat NYC-Centric and heavy on a certain type of info relating to the theme, so don't come back and complain about that. I did not find the non-theme answers dated. In fact sometimes I thought, that was a thing way back then?

The only TRUCKER song I know comes via an old boyfriend and is completely NSFW or the NYT, so I’ll hum it to myself and thanks for the memory.

Yes, an easier Sunday than the average, though there were a couple of areas that were a tad chewy; 59D crossing 71D, another unknown US product to go with the jingle earlier in the week comes to mind. You do like to keep us furrin types on our toes!

Didn’t clock the 10-4 lengths of the answers til Wordplay. Now that’s clever. I got the lingo but not the DAY. I don’t think it’s a thing here, plus we call them Lorry Drivers, so, yeah.

This is what I call a constructor’s puzzle. The constructor set herself an amazing challenge and pulled it off in impressive fashion with a grid that’s beautiful to behold. 

As for the solving experience?
Let’s just say that it wasn’t as impressive, for this particular solver.
Truckin' https://youtu.be/h_bwoXuUGho?si=acTjII22uKLh_ymX

Well, @Steve L already linked the only appropriate song tribute to this puzzle, so I should add any, but will anyway-- Here's the song I used to hum to myself, on those long-haul trips across the Egyptian desert: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ay9WwmhSdjk&list=RDay9WwmhSdjk&start_radio=1 Surprised how many people were thrown by the FICO/ARCO crossing--the latter comes up all the time! Wanna know the difference between pizzicato and arco? Let Maurice demonstrate: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ieRQyyPowH0&t=461s (second "chapter," if the link doesn't take you there immediately)

The "electronic music" guy gave me fits and was almost the last completion in the grid.  I spelt the Egyptian god ATON, not ATEN, and that was a serious ROAD block, along with how to style Beyonce and Harry...  
My first entry:  MORTON SALT (Iodized Sea Salt is available).

I also used this Abbr for CAPTain,  and had to "fix" it in order to get the medical specialist...

I certainly had a better time today.  Yesterday I just wasn't up to doing Look-Up-Everything....
I count 22 x 22 for the puzzle. More grid for your bucks!

"Sputnik-oh-nee?" I asked, befuddled
"Sputnik One," my long-suffering mate clarified from her position doubled over in pain with an unspecified GI ailment. I'm thankful she retained the faculties to manage my foolishness.

Such a gorgeous grid and a super fun solve. Really enjoyed this puzzle! My only nit to pick is that I think there are a million ways to clue DOVE and stripping the turtle- from the song's doves is an odd way to do it. I guess it's a swans-a-swimming misdirect, but we ducked that by having already filled in SIDE GLANCE when we came upon it. The glut of four-letter biblical boys had us grumbling too, but we're working on mnemonics to try and remember everyone's parentage for future puzzles.
I still remember being in 5th grade on October 4, 1957 when Miss Quain announced that Russia had put a satellite into orbit around Earth.

Lovely! Speedy but fun, and I loved the 10- or 4-letter constraint topped with a dazzling grid.

I've whined about proper nouns too much lately, and this constructor handled them perfectly. I'd never heard of LAKE ITASCA but was totally able to get it with crossers. I'd always thought of ESTD as being "established," never "estimated." TIL it could be either!

Thank you for the fun Sunday puzzle

Absolutely loved this one. I literally said “oh!” out loud when I saw the very pleasing symmetrical grid. The slow reveal of the reason for its beauty was fun and I didn’t fully get it until the revealer.

TIL the history of the MORTONSALT tagline. Morton was the first to add an anti-caking agent (magnesium carbonate) to keep their salt free-flowing even in high humidity conditions.  The brilliant ad-men tweaked the adage “It never rains, but it pours” to the tagline “When it rains, it pours”, and over time that tagline itself replaced the older adage to become the common idiom used today. 

And as a kid, I thought there was nothing other than Morton (brand) salt.
A cream puff of a puzzle. Grazie!
The cluing for 14D might be the most abysmally poor choice I've ever seen. How was that selected? There are so many other definitions of "difference".
Fun puzzle that I chipped away at over a few sessions, although I had no clue that the theme was a thing! 🚛

Today is our 51st anniversary and we’re still truckin’ on down the road. Fun puzzle and was stumped on “reflective post” so I cheated a little, googled it and presto…puzzle solved. Word Guides works every time!

I see many found this one too easy but xwstats shows it as Average. Me? I solved it 30% slower than usual. Just to be an oddball.

I went through the top 3/4 quickly and then got bogged down in the bottom corners. Early on I thought the across clue for son of Adam and Eve was Abel, so when I got to the down clue I confidently put Cain. Which gave me _cKEITASCA. Care to ask how long before I realized I no longer had Abel above and he was free and available??

I dithered around in this corner for a full 10 minutes before taking everything out except for DEATH and NOIR and finally seeing myself ABOARD. 

Then in the bottom right I wanted ___CbERDAY, so that held me up another 10 minutes.

(I loved the puzzle, even though it appears I created my own crunch.)
Excellent debut puzzle! I really enjoyed it!

When seeing today's grid, I'll bet many others besides just me wondered what this puzzle might bring.  Turned out to be a  nice theme, though not a particularly difficult Sunday.  My time was 31% less than average.  Enjoyable nonetheless.

(2nd attempt to post.  I'm guessing the acronym I used to express astonishment must have been a no-no.
Brava, congrats on the debut!

One more puzzle find. Another quite unusual one. A Sunday from April 4, 1999 by Richard Silvestri with the title "That Woman." A couple of theme clue and answer examples: "Angel Seeker?" CHERUBSCOUT "The plume that's mightier than the sword?" FEATHEROFSTRENGTH "Kin to a kingfish?" LORDOFTHEHERRINGS And a couple of other theme answers. SMELLARATHER VAMPIREBATHER HALFWITHERS Here's that link: https://www.xwordinfo.com/Crossword?date=4/4/1999&h=14d ...
Brava! Can’t wait for your next work of art! 🎨🖌️

Thank you for this brilliant and simply beautiful grid, Kathryn -- and a DEBUT to boot! Your clever clues and stunning supersymmetry even included my favorite Hall of Fame Red Sox catcher. I hope this will be the START OF AN ERA so that we'll see a lot more from you!👏🏼😊👏🏼

Not my favorite Sunday ever, but I enjoyed the unique grid design. And for all you truckers solving this at some Flying J or a rest area, thanks for what you're doing, and watch out for the idiots on the road.
Really really impressive construction!! But imo not very interesting to solve.
Great theme and execution. Enjoyed looking at the "supersymmetric" grid design before I even started today's puzzle.

So....   9A "Other sock" isn't right?  Har!!

That makes no sense to me. Most of my socks are MATEless. 

Found this to be a very enjoyable solve on a lovely grid! 

And I definitely appreciate the shout out to good ole LAKEITASCA. If you ever get the opportunity, be sure to stop in and walk across the head waters of the Mighty Mississippi. Love it!
Beautiful grid.  It reminds me of a quilt.
A good one!!

Too many reasons to count why I really disliked this puzzle!

The clues trying to be be clever, we're not. The terms in the grid were excessively random (older pipes! 🙄). 

I feel the whole thing came across as unpolished. I know others will have different opinions, but this puzzle rubbed me the wrong way on so many levels. 

As a post script I finished in better than average Sunday time, so difficulty was not one of them.
This was a beautiful and amazing puzzle. Loved solving it! More like this, please.
I knew I was in for some fun when I saw the grid. It did not disappoint. And I loved learning the revealer, makes perfect sense, like Dolly Day or pie day!
53A could not be "TOLL" if/since 18A is/was (already) "TOLL."

Loved this puzzle, both the layout and the clues.  I was struck by its visual appeal as soon as I opened it and the fun, creative, and just challenging enough fill made my Sunday.  Thank you for a great debut puzzle, I look forward to seeing your next piece of art.

I completed this without look ups. I wish I would have just ended my streak by not starting. 

 This was the most annoying, boring Sunday puzzle ever. So disappointing, Sundays are usually my favorite puzzle of the week. There is usually so much creativity, challenge and generally a fun puzzle. 

ABUDHABIAN?

That says it all. I am disappointed with myself for wasting my time with this. 

Rating:
3/10
What an unsatisfying slog.

Interesting that people are saying this was hard; I set a new personal record (under 25 minutes when my Sunday average is about an hour). I guess sometimes things just click. I found it kind of fun, and appreciate that designing it must have been a challenge!
Cmon admit it someone else did solarfarts also…

Wow! This puzzle must have taken a whole year to create. Very impressive! 

I guess it takes all kinds. Some of the puzzles people say were a breeze have been very hard for me, and unlike those who found this one a slog, I found it relatively easy and A LOT OF FUN!
Really fun and unique! I appreciate the creator effort this must have taken.
A truly amazing creation. Congratulations on your debut  Kathryn!
My first solved Sunday puzzle! 1:42 😅
Can someone explain ANON to me? That was my last answer to go in and I was bracing for “oh crumbs”, but surprisingly it worked!
Challenging but also lots of fun :-) Busy day (and big puzzle) so it's late in the day. But it was a good puzzle day for me.
Beautiful - fitting for a graph theorist!
Wow, I haven’t even started but was struck by the beauty of the construction.  Amazing.
19 across is ICES, not ICED as the article says.

I also thought this was a very elegant puzzle 🧩. 
Some answers surprised me and made me laugh. I forget which ones, I’m ashamed to say, even looking at the finished puzzle.

I don’t usually notice grids but going back to look at this it is simply amazing and very satisfying! I can definitely believe this is by a mathematician.

Currently on a Hawaii cruise so I appreciated ABOARD SHIP and NENE. Hoping we get to see one!

I don't enjoy puzzles that are so segmented so I struggled but glad others enjoyed it! 

Aloha
Stunning! I’m in awe.
It was a clever & fun puzzle, but "ring around the doze-y" was maybe the worst clue I've seen.

Impressive debut - eloquent execution. I haven’t been commenting for a while because life has been busy, but I had to jump on and congratulate Kathryn Bale. Kudos on this grid. I loved it. 
Over and out
Wonderful puzzle!  Very enjoyable.  I love these puzzles that make you shift your brain into at least 3rd gear.  An inspiring debut.
“Bleh” rather than “blah” in the southwest corner tripped me up. *facepalm*
It appears to me as like a sudoku puzzle; I shall employ the corresponding solving method: guessing.
Clever, challenging, and fun puzzle today.
I can't say enough about the masterful conceptual levels with this one. The publication date, truckers, Sputnik I and the grid itself. Great interwoven alignments.

Visually elegant and impressive, like a snowflake or crystal! I finished in 25:17 which was almost 8 minutes better than my average, but it didn’t feel like much of a victory - the plethora of 4L words were relatively easy, while many of the 10L felt awkward or forced. OLDERPIPES?! C’mon.
Loved it! Beautiful and fun. My favourite answers were DIFFERENCE, ROADMARKER, DATINGAPPS, BESS, OLDERPIPES and PIES - fun hints and they all brought me joy when I got them. Thank you Kathryn!

I did this puzzle in the print magazine from a hospital bed, using my left hand and unable to read my writing well, because I’m a righty. A nasty fall broke my shoulder and kneecap. @Edwin

This seems to be coming up a lot, and I can refer you the comments I wrote yesterday about how AI just isn’t there yet to create puzzles of this caliber.

But I’ll add to that. Let’s say it did? So what? First of all, this is not “AI is taking someone’s job”. It’s nobody’s job to create NY Times puzzles. Sure we make a bit of money when it’s accepted but no one is making a living off of it (and in any case a human is going to submit it and a human is going to get paid.)

Second, this is not like a student submitting a term paper who is going to get a degree or a professor writing a thesis to promote his job. It’s not even like an artist submitting an AI work under his name where the issue is that it’s hard to tell what elements of the image were taken from other artists’ works (not that our brains don’t subtly do this all the time). It’s very easy  to calculate a freshness score for a puzzle to see how often the entries were used, look to see if the theme was used before, and see how many original clues there are. So an AI generated puzzle would be probably easy to spot and if not then so what? It has created an original puzzle and if so and it’s as fun and creative as one a human can do I’m overjoyed to solve it.

And this from a constructor, who believe me doesn’t want more competition, and isn’t planning to use AI (because the whole fun of doing it is to do it myself) and if I did, yeah, I’d go ahead and credit the AI. But in theory? No problem.
